evidence.title: Honda bullish about update for Aston Martin after F1 summer break
evidence.body: [e005:f01] Honda Racing chief Shintaro Orihara is optimistic about the remainder of Aston Martin's F1 season, issuing a positive update on their power unit. [e005:f02] Aston Martin brought 16 chassis upgrades to the Hungarian Grand Prix , with design legend Adrian Newey having worked tirelessly to try and develop the car since the start of 2026. [e005:f03] The Silverstone-based outfit had been squabbling with Cadillac on the back two rows of the grid for much of the 2026 season, struggling with both reliability and performance. [e005:f04] Article continues under video But the revised AMR26 that the team brought to the Hungaroring allowed them to take a step forward, with Lance Stroll and Fernando Alonso finishing 13th and 14th respectively in the race, a day after Alonso made it into Q2 for the first time this season. [e005:f05] During the weekend, Newey revealed there would be more upgrades coming to the chassis at the Italian and Azerbaijan Grands Prix later in the summer, but before then, something arguably even more exciting is coming for Aston Martin. [e005:f06] The team have been struggling with their Honda power unit for most of this year so far, but following the summer break, Honda will be unveiling an upgraded power unit at the Dutch Grand Prix. [e005:f07] That is the next race on the calendar, and Honda's upgrades are in part thanks to the FIA's additional development upgrade and opportunities (ADUO) scheme. [e005:f08] ADUO was brought in at the start of the year to help struggling power unit manufacturers amid the 2026 regulations reset, offering more time to manufacturers who are lagging behind the best power unit. [e005:f09] Honda have the worst-performing power unit, and were given two homologations in the first round of ADUO rulings, with the second ADUO period coming up after race 12 (the Dutch GP on August 23). [e005:f10] Orihara has issued some very confident updates on both Honda and Aston Martin's progress as the team look to move up the constructors' championship standings. [e005:f11] "In Hungary, we saw some pretty strong pace and now we’re back in the mix," Orihara told AS . [e005:f12] "Any improvement is crucial to catching up with the rival car, and introducing the new engine at Zandvoort is essential.

evidence.title: Debt woes cancel out Aston Martin’s H1 revenue gains
evidence.body: [e003:f01] By Stewart Burnett By Stewart Burnett July 29, 2026 Aston Martin’s turnaround remains stuck in the same bind it has been in for months: growing revenue can’t outrun widening losses. [e003:f02] The luxury automaker’s pre-tax loss grew to £154.2m (US$205m) in H1 2026, from £140.8m a year earlier, even as revenue ballooned 38% to £628.6m and wholesale volumes climbed 21% to 2,331 vehicles. [e003:f03] The Valhalla hybrid hypercar, which entered production four years later than planned, is doing much of the the heavy lifting behind that revenue growth. [e003:f04] Despite Aston Martin delivering just 220 of the £850,000 cars during H1, this was sufficient to push Q2 revenue up 62% to £358.2m due to high per-unit margins. [e003:f05] Aston Martin said it expects Valhalla deliveries to accelerate further in the second half. [e003:f06] Chief Executive Adrian Hallmark called the results evidence the company remains “on track” for a full-year material improvement over 2025. [e003:f07] Of course, his comments come against an increasingly fraught backdrop: net debt rose to £1.54bn by end-June, carrying double-digit interest rates that are consuming income faster than Aston Martin’s operational gains can offset. [e003:f08] A £550m financing deal, struck earlier in July with BlackRock-owned HPS Investment Partners, is structured to bypass existing bondholders, and follows more than £600m already contributed by Executive Chair Chairman Lawrence Stroll’s consortium since he took control in 2020. [e003:f09] The results extend a difficult run for the British luxury brand: five profit warnings in just 18 months, February’s cut of 600 jobs accounting for roughly a fifth of the workforce, and a decision to defer its first battery-electric model into the 2030s while trimming five-year capital spending from £2bn to £1.7bn. [e003:f10] Full-year 2025 revenue had already fallen 21% to US$1.59bn, with a net loss of roughly US$666m, driven in large part by US tariffs and weakened Chinese demand. [e003:f11] Aston Martin’s Valhalla hypercar was delayed by almost four years Aston Martin has chosen to hold onto its full-year guidance, although it did flag ongoing risks from the Iran war’s impact on energy costs and supply chain disruptions. [e003:f12] Analysts remain wary of Aston Martin’s recovery prospects. [e003:f13] Despite the muted reception from analysts, shares rose 4% following the update. [e003:f14] Whether the Valhalla’s sales are sufficient to overcome a growing debt pile is entirely uncertain. [e003:f15] Aston Martin has resorted to increasingly drastic measures to keep the lights on in the last few years, and even the high-margin revenue claimed from its latest model is having little effect. [e003:f16] As it stands, the structuring of emergency financing specifically to bypass bondholders arguably says more about where things stand than the maintained guidance does. https:// Join our LinkedIn Group Let us help you understand the future of mobility " * " indicates required fields Welcome back , to continue browsing the site, please click here。

evidence.title: Baby steps: Nissan, Honda to team up for car software after fizzled merger
evidence.body: [e004:f01] While it's not the merger that would have seen Nissan and Honda become the fourth-largest automaker in the world, the rumored partnership will reportedly result in brands sharing ECUs. [e004:f02] Fast forward to near the end of July, Honda and Nissan are both considering jointly developing an operating system for software-defined vehicles (SDVs). [e004:f03] According to sources who are close to the matter, the OS will be based on Nissan's technology. [e004:f04] With SDVs now fast becoming standard in new automobiles, thanks to China's technology boom, cutting-edge software is now one of the growing aspects legacy automakers need to catch up on. [e004:f05] Combined with the fact that Chinese brands continue to develop and come up with high-tech vehicles, Japanese automakers have started to take notice. [e004:f06] Since a vehicle's OS is now one of the core technologies of next-generation automobiles, the OS also serves as an important basis for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and semi-autonomous driving capability. [e004:f07] With Nissan and Honda looking to jointly develop the next-generation vehicle software, both brands stand to benefit from it, while also improving development efficiency and lessening costs. [e004:f08] In recent years, Chinese brands have leapfrogged Japanese brands when it comes to vehicle software, such as infotainment and wireless connectivity features. [e004:f09] But it is perhaps in ADAS and semi-autonomous driving features where Chinese brands excelled. [e004:f10] If Honda and Nissan can work together to make their own next-generation software, both brands stand to benefit greatly. [e004:f11] For now, no exact specifics were mentioned by Honda or Nissan. [e004:f12] But given that both brands are considering joint development, perhaps they are still discussing important matters regarding the new OS. [e004:f13] Back in 2024, Nissan, Honda, and Mitsubishi signed a Memorandum of Understanding to jointly discuss a framework for further intelligence and electrification of automobiles, including advancing vehicle OS. [e004:f14] But since the merger didn't happen, part of the brands' plans fell through as well. [e004:f15] But with both brands now talking once more to jointly develop OS for SDVs, perhaps both automakers see they need to work together rather than compete with one another since Chinese automakers continue to dominate and excel in vehicle technology. [e004:f16] MD Marcus De Guzman • JUL 30, 2026 Auto News Look out Atto 3: MG S5 EV confirmed for PH market MG S5 will be MG Motor’s answer to the likes of the BYD Atto 3 and GAC Aion V MD Marcus De Guzman • JUL 30, 2026 Auto News All-new BMW iX3 Neue Klasse gets DOE EV recognition It looks like BMW Philippines is making the necessary preparations to launch all-new iX3 MD Marcus De Guzman • JUL 30, 2026 Auto News GAC launches GN6, E8 HEV, and GN8 PHEV three-row MPVs in PH GAC GN6, E8 HEV, and GN8 PHEV now available in PH MD Marcus De Guzman • JUL 29, 2026 Auto News Ford Territory Hybrid sales in PH breach 4,400 mark Ford Territory Hybrid total sales in PH market has reached 4,405 units A • JUL 29, 2026 Auto News Audi reveals 2027 Q9 flagship SUV with V6 diesel power 2027 Audi Q9 is the brand’s largest luxury SUV to date JL Jamil Lacuna • JUL 29, 2026。

evidence.title: ホンダ、４２３９億円赤字 ＥＶ損失響く、上場以来初
evidence.body: [e007:f01] 記者会見に臨むホンダの三部敏宏社長＝１４日午後、東京都新宿区 ホンダが１４日発表した２０２６年３月期連結決算は、純損益が４２３９億円の赤字だった。 [e007:f02] 赤字転落は１９５７年の上場以来、初めて。 [e007:f03] 電気自動車（ＥＶ）戦略の見直しに伴う巨額の関連損失が響いた。 [e007:f04] 同時に２７年３月期の連結業績予想も公表し、純損益が２６００億円の黒字に転換するとの見通しを示した。 [e007:f05] ２６年３月期の売上高は前期比０・５％増の２１兆７９６６億円だった。 [e007:f06] ＥＶ需要減少を受けた北米での新車種開発中止などによる関連損失は１兆５７７８億円に上った。 [e007:f07] 本業のもうけを示す営業損益も４１４３億円の赤字（前期は１兆２１３４億円の黒字）に転落した。 [e007:f08] ２５年３月期の純損益は８３５８億円の黒字だった。 [e007:f09] 東京都内で記者会見した三部敏宏社長は、赤字決算に「将来に損失を残さないため、経営の意思として計上した。 [e007:f10] ４０年までに新車を全てＥＶと燃料電池車（ＦＣＶ）にする「脱ガソリン車」の目標は「現実的ではない。

evidence.title: アステモ、新社長にホンダ四輪本部長の井上勝史氏 竹内弘平社長は退任 ホンダ四輪事業の立て直しを全面支援
evidence.body: [e003:f01] 6月25日の定時株主総会と7月1日の臨時取締役会を経て正式決定する。 [e003:f02] 井上氏はホンダの欧州や中国の責任者などを経て、電動事業開発部門のトップ、昨年4月には四輪事業本部長に就いたが、6月にホンダの取締役退任が決まっていた。 [e003:f03] ホンダは日立が保有するアステモの株式21％分を取得し、出資比率を61％に引き上げて子会社化する予定でいる。 [e003:f04] 電気自動車（EV）戦略の失敗で業績が悪化している同社は、ソフトウエア・デファインド・ビークル（SDV）やハイブリッド車（HV）に重点を置く方針に軌道修正した。 [e003:f05] アステモはSDVや電動車向けを含むパワートレイン技術に強い。 [e003:f06] ホンダはアステモの先進技術や開発力を高く評価しており、連携を強化する。 [e003:f07] 今回、ホンダの四輪事業部門で実務経験の長い井上氏にトップ交代することで、ホンダの四輪事業の立て直しについて、系列サプライヤーとして全面的に支える体制を整える。 [e003:f08] 竹内社長もホンダ出身で、2023年7月にアステモの社長に就いた。 [e003:f09] ホンダでは財務・管理部門が長く、アステモでは前任社長時代の品質問題を踏まえた対応や財務体質の改善、株式公開に向けた準備などを担ってきた。 [e003:f10] 井上勝史氏（いのうえ・かつし）1986年3月、横浜国立大学経営学部卒、同年4月ホンダ入社。 [e003:f11] 2015年ホンダカーズインディア社長、16年ホンダ執行役員、欧州地域本部長、20年常務執行役員兼中国本部長兼本田技研工業（中国）投資総経理兼本田技研科技（中国）総経理、23年執行役専務兼電動事業開発本部長、25年取締役執行役専務兼四輪事業本部長兼リスクマネジメントオフィサー、25年6月同取締役執行役専務、26年4月同取締役。

evidence.title: Honda bullish about update for Aston Martin after F1 summer break
evidence.body: [e004:f01] Honda Racing chief Shintaro Orihara is optimistic about the remainder of Aston Martin's F1 season, issuing a positive update on their power unit. [e004:f02] Aston Martin brought 16 chassis upgrades to the Hungarian Grand Prix , with design legend Adrian Newey having worked tirelessly to try and develop the car since the start of 2026. [e004:f03] The Silverstone-based outfit had been squabbling with Cadillac on the back two rows of the grid for much of the 2026 season, struggling with both reliability and performance. [e004:f04] Article continues under video But the revised AMR26 that the team brought to the Hungaroring allowed them to take a step forward, with Lance Stroll and Fernando Alonso finishing 13th and 14th respectively in the race, a day after Alonso made it into Q2 for the first time this season. [e004:f05] During the weekend, Newey revealed there would be more upgrades coming to the chassis at the Italian and Azerbaijan Grands Prix later in the summer, but before then, something arguably even more exciting is coming for Aston Martin. [e004:f06] The team have been struggling with their Honda power unit for most of this year so far, but following the summer break, Honda will be unveiling an upgraded power unit at the Dutch Grand Prix. [e004:f07] That is the next race on the calendar, and Honda's upgrades are in part thanks to the FIA's additional development upgrade and opportunities (ADUO) scheme. [e004:f08] ADUO was brought in at the start of the year to help struggling power unit manufacturers amid the 2026 regulations reset, offering more time to manufacturers who are lagging behind the best power unit. [e004:f09] Honda have the worst-performing power unit, and were given two homologations in the first round of ADUO rulings, with the second ADUO period coming up after race 12 (the Dutch GP on August 23). [e004:f10] Orihara has issued some very confident updates on both Honda and Aston Martin's progress as the team look to move up the constructors' championship standings. [e004:f11] "In Hungary, we saw some pretty strong pace and now we’re back in the mix," Orihara told AS . [e004:f12] "Any improvement is crucial to catching up with the rival car, and introducing the new engine at Zandvoort is essential.

Ferrari, il mistero della Hypercar: cosa significano i post sui social
evidence.body: [e003:f01] Ha collaborato con varie testate online spaziando tra Esports e motori. [e003:f02] Pubblicato: 28 Luglio 2026 16:04 Chiedi a Virgilio Ferrari Media Centre Dopo i post sui social, Ferrari ha concluso una giornata di test con la 499P in vista della stagione 2027. [e003:f03] Due post sui social, una grafica in bianco e nero e una Hypercar completamente camuffata. [e003:f04] E, come spesso accade nel mondo Ferrari, il silenzio sembra essere diventato parte della notizia. [e003:f05] Indice Il gioco degli indizi Due post pubblicati sui social hanno infatti acceso la curiosità degli appassionati di motorsport. [e003:f06] Nella foto si intuiscono proporzioni e architettura generale, ma i dettagli sono volutamente cancellati. [e003:f07] Prima l’astrazione, poi il prototipo Una sequenza che potrebbe essere semplicemente una campagna social costruita per generare attenzione, ma che lascia aperta una possibilità. [e003:f08] Il nome da cui partire è inevitabilmente quello della Ferrari 499P . [e003:f09] Ferrari, sviluppo continuo Il mondo delle Hypercar vive di sviluppo continuo. [e003:f10] La 499P del 2026 è già stata oggetto di interventi e adattamenti ma l’ipotesi di un ulteriore sviluppo non sarebbe, di per sé, sorprendente. [e003:f11] Dai primi post non emerge una conferma ufficiale che si tratti di una nuova Hypercar e questa zona grigia accende l’interesse. [e003:f12] Prove di futuro a Monza La Ferrari ha portato in pista sull’ Autodromo Nazionale di Monza la sua 499P per una sessione di test in vista della stagione 2027 . [e003:f13] Ma oggi, nell’era dei social, anche un prototipo mascherato può diventare un contenuto. [e003:f14] La grafica del primo post sembrava avere una parentela visiva con il camouflage della vettura mostrata nel secondo. [e003:f15] La prossima mossa, la più importante La Ferrari 499P ha già un posto speciale nella storia recente del Cavallino rampante e qualsiasi novità legata alla Hypercar assume un peso particolare. [e003:f16] Il conto alla rovescia, almeno sui social, sembra es。

SpaceX wins $1.6 billion in launch orders for military satellite networks
evidence.body: [e001:f01] Credit: SpaceX WASHINGTON — The U.S. [e001:f02] Space Force awarded SpaceX two launch task orders worth $1.6 billion to deploy military satellite constellations, marking the largest publicly announced batch of missions yet under the National Security Space Launch Phase 3 program. [e001:f03] The award covers 18 Falcon 9 launches from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California through the end of 2027 in support of the Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, a collection of satellite programs intended to improve how the military detects, tracks and communicates information about threats in near real time. [e001:f04] The task orders reinforce SpaceX’s central role in the military’s next-generation satellite networks. [e001:f05] Beyond providing the launches, the company is building two of the portfolio’s largest satellite systems under separate multibillion-dollar contracts, giving it responsibility for both placing the constellations in orbit and supplying key elements of the architecture itself. [e001:f06] Space Based Sensing and Targeting is one of the Space Force’s newly established acquisition portfolios . [e001:f07] It oversees the Space Development Agency’s Tracking Layer, a constellation of infrared satellites designed to detect and track advanced missile threats; the Space Data Network Backbone, an optically linked communications network being built by SpaceX to move large volumes of military data across the Joint Force; and the Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator program, another SpaceX-led constellation intended to track aircraft and other airborne targets from orbit. [e001:f08] SpaceX previously received contracts worth $2.29 billion for the Space Data Network Backbone and $4.16 billion for the Airborne Moving Target Indicator system. [e001:f09] The launch award is the largest publicly disclosed order under National Security Space Launch Phase 3 Lane 1, the Space Force’s commercial-style procurement program for lower-risk national security missions that allows pre-qualified providers to compete for individual launch orders without completing the military’s most demanding certification process. [e001:f10] The contract also follows the Space Force’s decision earlier this month to raise the Phase 3 Lane 1 contract ceiling to $17 billion from $5.6 billion, reflecting expectations that military launch demand will grow substantially faster than originally anticipated. [e001:f11] Completing 18 launches by the end of 2027 will require a sustained campaign averaging roughly one mission a month from Vandenberg, depending on the timing of satellite deliveries. [e001:f12] That cadence also highlights the gap between the number of companies eligible to compete for national security launches and those capable of executing them today. [e001:f13] For now, SpaceX remains the only company with the combination of launch frequency, operational Falcon 9 rockets and West Coast infrastructure needed to support a campaign of this scale. [e001:f14] Eric Zarybnisky, the Space Force’s acting portfolio acquisition executive for space access, said the awards also demonstrate how quickly the Lane 1 contracting approach can move. evidence.body: [e006:f01] SpaceX has secured $1.6 billion in U.S. [e006:f02] Space Force contracts to launch 18 Falcon 9 missions supporting the military’s Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio through the end of missions were awarded under two task orders through the National Security Space Launch (NSSL) Phase 3 Lane 1 program, which allows multiple commercial launch providers to compete for national security missions. [e006:f03] All 18 launches will lift off from Vandenberg Space Force Base in satellites will support the Space-Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which uses spacecraft to detect and track airborne threats while relaying near real-time information to U.S. military latest award adds to a string of major Space Force contracts secured by the Elon Musk-led pioneering aerospace company this year. [e006:f04] In May, the company won roughly $6.45 billion in Space Force awards supporting satellite constellations for tracking airborne targets and enabling near real-time communications between missile warning sensors and contract further expands SpaceX’s role in U.S. military space programs as the Pentagon increases investment in space-based sensing and tracking capabilities. [e006:f05] Those capabilities are expected to support the Trump administration’s proposed Golden Dome missile defense initiative, which aims to build a layered missile defense network using space- and ground-based military launchesThe U.S. [e006:f06] Space Force said the task orders will strengthen the nation’s space-based sensing and targeting capabilities while speeding up launch procurement for national security missions.“Sensing and targeting of airborne objects from space and providing near-real-time communications across the Joint Force, are vital to the defense of our nation,” said Space Force Col. [e006:f07] Eric Zarybnisky, acting portfolio acquisition executive for Space contracts were awarded under the dual-lane structure introduced in NSSL Phase 3, which is intended to speed up procurement while maintaining competition among launch providers.“We have set an unprecedented two-month acquisition timeline under the Phase 3 Lane 1 contract from requirement identification to award,” Zarybnisky said. [e006:f08] “Ultimately, this timeline results in the speed our warfighter demands more than ever before.”According to the Space Force, the timeline includes one month for launch providers to prepare and submit proposals before contracts are defense satellitesThe Falcon 9 missions will deploy satellites supporting the SBST portfolio, improving the military’s ability to detect and track airborne threats from orbit while providing near real-time communications across the Joint contracts form part of the Space Force’s broader effort to modernize national security launch services by working with commercial launch providers capable of delivering critical missions on accelerated National Security Space Launch Phase 3 program is structured to provide the Department of Defense with reliable access to space while encouraging greater participation from the commercial launch industry. [e006:f09] Under the Lane 1 framework, eligible providers compete for individual task orders rather than receiving fixed launch Space Force’s Space Systems Command, which manages an annual acquisition budget of about $15.6 billion for the Department of War, oversees military space acquisitions and launch services, with the NSSL program serving as its primary vehicle for procuring national security launches.

evidence.title: SpaceX Wins $1.6 Billion Space Force Order for 18 Falcon 9 Launches
evidence.body: [e004:f01] Space Force to fly 18 Falcon 9 missions through 2027. [e004:f02] The service announced the award on Wednesday. ! [e004:f03] [Image 1: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifts off from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on July 14, 2022, with a Cargo Dragon spacecraft aboard for SpaceX's 25th resupply mission to the International Space Station. [e004:f04] Credits: NASA TV ### **Key Takeaways** * The Space Force assigned 18 Falcon 9 missions to SpaceX across two task orders worth $1.6 billion, all flying from Vandenberg Space Force Base by the end of 2027. * The payloads support the Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which tracks airborne threats and relays near real-time data to U.S. forces. * SpaceX has now collected at least $7 billion in Pentagon contracts this year as the Trump administration builds out its Golden Dome missile defense shield. [e004:f05] Both task orders fall under the National Security Space Launch Phase 3 Lane 1 program. [e004:f06] That is the flagship procurement vehicle where SpaceX, United Launch Alliance, Blue Origin and other approved American launch firms compete for individual mission assignments rather than fixed allocations. [e004:f07] Officials described an “unprecedented two-month acquisition timeline” from identifying the requirement to signing the award, according to acquisition official Eric Zarybnisky. [e004:f08] The service has spent years trying to buy spacecraft and launches faster. ## What the Satellites Do The Space Based Sensing and Targeting programme puts spacecraft in orbit to spot and follow aircraft, drones and other moving objects, then pipe that picture down to commanders quickly. [e004:f09] SpaceX already won more than $6 billion in late May to build satellites for that effort and a companion communications constellation. [e004:f10] Eighteen launches in roughly two years means about one Falcon 9 leaving California every month. [e004:f11] The company has spent years lifting its flight rate, and its [expanded launch capacity at Cape Canaveral](https:// and Vandenberg exists precisely to absorb work like this. ## The Competition Problem SpaceX keeps a wide lead over its rivals for Pentagon business, and some lawmakers have said openly that the Department of Defense leans too hard on one vendor. [e004:f12] When two of three approved providers cannot fly on demand, task orders drift to the one that can. ## Golden Dome Money The award lands inside a much bigger project. [e004:f13] The award also arrives weeks after the Space Force lifted the spending ceiling on Lane 1 by more than $11 billion, and this is the first task order issued under that [newly expanded contract vehicle](https:// Washington is not just buying launches. [e004:f14] Military space used to run on a handful of exquisite, expensive satellites launched rarely. [e004:f15] Officials framed the sensing mission itself in those terms, calling the ability to track airborne objects from orbit and pass data across the joint force [vital to national defense](https:// Other countries have noticed the economics. [e004:f16] China recovered an orbital-class booster at sea this month, its own [bid to lower launch costs](https:// for a fast-growing satellite fleet. _Written by [Alius Noreika](https://。

evidence.title: SpaceX Falcon 9 Stands Ready for NROL-95 National Security Launch
evidence.body: [e005:f01] The NROL-95 mission carries classified national security payloads for the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) and U.S. [e005:f02] Space Force Space Launch Delta 45 and Space Systems Command. [e005:f03] Source: @SpaceX — July 28, 2026 Mission Details Liftoff is scheduled for 3:09 a.m. [e005:f04] The payload is classified, with the NRO describing it only as a national security asset. [e005:f05] NROL-95 is the NRO's fourth launch of 2026 , following NROL-105, NROL-172, and NROL-179 earlier this year. [e005:f06] It also marks the third NRO mission SpaceX has flown under the National Security Space Launch (NSSL) Phase 2 contract, a deal awarded to SpaceX in August 2020 that cemented the company as a primary launch provider for U.S. intelligence and defense payloads. [e005:f07] Booster and Hardware Detail Value Rocket Falcon 9 Block 5 Booster B1096 (7th flight) Last Flight May 15, 2026 Booster Landing Landing Zone 2 (LZ-2), Cape Canaveral Launch Site SLC-40, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station Fairing Recovery Planned for reuse Liftoff July 30, 2026 — 3:09 a.m. [e005:f08] The plan calls for a return-to-launch-site landing at LZ-2 — a relatively quick turnaround profile that SpaceX has refined into a near-routine operation. [e005:f09] Fairing recovery is also planned, continuing SpaceX's push to make every reusable component count across its launch manifest. [e005:f10] The Bigger Picture The NSSL Phase 2 contract, awarded in 2020, split the U.S. government's national security launch business between SpaceX and ULA. [e005:f11] Four NRO launches in a single calendar year reflects both the growing demand for intelligence-gathering assets in orbit and SpaceX's capacity to service that demand at a pace no other provider currently matches. [e005:f12] As the NSSL Phase 3 contract competition advances, each successful classified mission adds to SpaceX's operational track record — a factor that weighs heavily in government source selection decisions. [e005:f13] All launch schedules remain subject to weather and range availability. [e005:f14] Follow our SpaceX coverage for launch outcome updates. evidence.body: [e007:f01] SpaceX provided this photo of fairing art for NROL-95 SpaceX is targeting 3:09 am ET Thursday for the launch of Falcon 9 carrying the NROL-95 payload on a classified mission SpaceX provided this photo of fairing art for NROL-95 SpaceX is targeting 3:09 am ET Thursday for the launch of Falcon 9 carrying the NROL-95 payload on a classified mission for the National Reconnaissance Office. [e007:f02] The launch will be from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. [e007:f03] A backup opportunity is available at 2:55 am Friday if the launch is delayed. [e007:f04] SpaceX plans to start its live webcast about 10-15 minutes before liftoff. [e007:f05] The NRO said the flight is its fourth launch of 2026 and its second this year flown in partnership with Space Systems Command. [e007:f06] The mission was assigned to SpaceX under the National Security Space Launch Phase 2 contract. [e007:f07] Tonight's flight is planned as a Return to Launch Site profile, meaning that after Booster B1096 completes its ascent duties, it will land at Cape Canaveral's Landing Zone 2. [e007:f08] As such, the Space Coast can expect a sonic boom from the returning booster. [e007:f09] NROL-95 Launch At a Glance Go for Launch Launch Date Thursday, July 30, 2026 Launch Window 2:37–3:21 a.m. [e007:f10] EDT Mission NROL-95 Launch Provider SpaceX Rocket Falcon 9 Block 5 Launch Site Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida Launch Pad Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) Destination Not publicly disclosed Payload Classified payload for the U.S. [e007:f11] Launch times remain subject to change because of weather, range operations and mission requirements. [e007:f12] Publicly available launch schedules list the destination as "unknown." In short, the public does not meet the need-to-know criteria for this classified information, and as such, it will not be disclosed. [e007:f13] As a rule, NRO does not disclose the spacecraft, the target orbit, or the intelligence mission behind a launch designated NROL. [e007:f14] Four NRO launches in a single year says as much about demand for orbital intelligence as it does about the cadence one provider can sustain from the Cape. [e007:f15] With Blue Origin and ULA offline due to problems with their launch systems, that leaves SpaceX as the only game in town. [e007:f16] Spaceflight Now will have coverage of the launch starting about one hour before liftoff on Youtube: link Next Space Flight an app for iOS and Android phones, has a real-time countdown clock that is accurate to a second, give or take.

evidence.title: Starlink Officially Launches Operations in Iraq After Historic Licensing Agreement Signed in Washington
evidence.body: [e001:f01] As Shafaq News reported on July 17, 2026, the licensing agreement was signed at the US Chamber of Commerce in Washington during a ceremony attended by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Baligh Abu Kalal, executive chairman of Iraq's Communications and Media Commission. [e001:f02] The signing took place during al-Zaidi's visit to Washington, where he also held meetings with US officials including President Donald Trump, making the Starlink agreement one of the most concrete commercial outcomes of the prime minister's American engagements this month. [e001:f03] Iraq Business News confirmed on July 21, 2026, that the CMC said the authorization forms part of its efforts to regulate satellite internet services within an approved legal and regulatory framework, to preserve digital sovereignty and align Iraq with global developments in the telecommunications sector. [e001:f04] Abu Kalal stated that the newly issued license paves the way for the legal and regulated rollout of Starlink's satellite internet network across Iraq, giving consumers and businesses access to secure and high-speed connectivity. [e001:f05] Residential service in Iraq will start at 131,500 Iraqi dinars per month, approximately $100, for the entry-level 100 Mbps plan. [e001:f06] The CMC said it is actively working to ensure subscription costs remain accessible for Iraqi consumers, acknowledging that Starlink equipment and monthly fees are considered expensive in comparable markets across the region. [e001:f07] Whether the Iraqi government has negotiated special tariffs, subsidies, or payment structures as part of the licensing framework will likely determine the speed at which ordinary Iraqis are able to access the service following its formal launch. [e001:f08] Starlink Availability Coverage Service Shows on the map for Iraq Territory (Starlink Official website) The strategic significance of the agreement extends well beyond basic internet access. [e001:f09] Starlink operates through a constellation of low Earth orbit satellites that deliver high-speed internet by bypassing the ground-based infrastructure constraints that have limited connectivity in Iraq for decades. [e001:f10] As The Insight International reported on July 19, 2026, Iraq has long struggled with unreliable internet services due to aging infrastructure, capacity constraints, and the compounding effects of years of conflict. [e001:f11] The timing of the agreement also carries broader geopolitical resonance. [e001:f12] As Dinar Detectives reported on June 19, 2026, Iraqi Prime Minister al-Zaidi and US Special Presidential Envoy for Iraq Tom Barrack both welcomed the approval of Starlink's operating license, framing it within the context of Iraq's deepening economic and digital partnership with Washington. [e001:f13] The license approval aligns with Iraq's push toward a cashless economy, with the Central Bank of Iraq having pushed for full government cashless operations, a digital transformation for which Starlink's connectivity infrastructure provides a critical enabling layer, particularly in areas where banking and digital payment networks have historically been inaccessible. [e001:f14] The licensing agreement also arrives at a moment that adds particular commercial weight to Musk's portfolio. [e001:f15] As Reuters confirmed via Iraqi state media on July 17, 2026, the agreement was signed formally between the Iraqi Communications and Media Commission and Starlink, making Iraq one of SpaceX's most significant new market entries in the Middle East, a region whose satellite internet penetration remains well below its potential given the combination of geography, infrastructure gaps, and large underserved populations. [e001:f16] Starlink's parent company SpaceX completed its landmark initial public offering at a valuation of $1.77 trillion earlier this month, making Musk the world's first trillionaire on paper, as Kurdistan 24 previously reported.
